summary.headline: 9 of 27 documented 99214/99215 charts support a lower level
summary.rationale: 1000000203 billed 99215 on 1.9% of 1,112 claims against an expected 4.2% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score -1.62; plain z-score vs peers -1.09). 62% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 30 claims. Of 2 documented 99215 claims, 1 (50%) were documented below the billed level, against 54% for the comparison providers. Note checks on 30 returned notes (share showing each sign): problems 23%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 3%. No audit trail was received. 1 of 19 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim. The random sample of 30 charts beats the pooled peer rate of 15% (p=0.016). The recovery lower bound is $289, above the $276 demand cost. The 99215 share is low, so the concern is 99214 inflation. Note signals do not look inflated. Examples: C0099927: billed 99215; documented MDM level moderate, 30 minutes. C0099087: billed 99215, patient aged 51 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0099140: billed 99215, patient aged 23 with 1 chronic condition(s) (type 2 diabetes). C0099257: billed 99215, patient aged 38 with 1 chronic condition(s) (hypertension).
next_steps: Request the full charts for C0099927, C0099087, C0099140 and have a certified coder re-score each against the current E/M rules (medical decision making or total time).
If the re-scoring confirms the pattern, review the random sample in the recovery packet's sampling plan before any overpayment estimate; do not extrapolate from a targeted sample.
Look at the notes themselves: 23% address fewer problems than their level implies and 3% were signed late; request the audit trail for C0099927, C0099087, C0099140.
